subject: Order form redlines — invoicing cadence & tax handling
messages:

To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Nina Sato <nina.sato@cloudly.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order form — redlines and a few clarifying asks

Logan / team,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA + order form. Our legal and finance teams reviewed and attached a consolidated redline (Cloudly_OrderForm_Redlines_v1.pdf). A few items we need clarity on before we can route to procurement: 

- Invoicing cadence: we'd prefer monthly invoices with net 45, but the draft suggests quarterly invoicing with net 60. Can you confirm Redwood's flexibility here?
- Minimum commit scheduling: we want the minimum commit to be pro-rated by calendar month if the start date is mid-month. Current language is ambiguous.
- Taxes / withholding: EU entities will likely require withholding language. Who signs tax responsibility on gross vs. net? We need an explicit clause.
- PO flow: we generate a PO for the first invoice. Any required invoice fields we should include? (we attached our PO instructions).

We'd like to avoid a long back-and-forth. Would your team be available for a 30-min sync tomorrow to resolve the above and agree on final redlines?

Best,
Ari Kaplan
Head of Procurement, Cloudly
ari@cloudly.com

Ari — thanks for the detailed redline and the PO instructions. Appreciate the clear asks.

Short answers up front: we can be flexible on invoicing cadence and net terms in most commercial cases; minimum-commit proration is doable but needs the exact wording in the order form appendix; tax withholding will need explicit carveouts per entity (we do not want to be unexpectedly liable for withholding in EU).

I'll loop in Kimberly and Karthik to propose contract language and confirm how finance wants the invoice fields.

Proposed next steps (30-min sync):
- Today: Kimberly to propose redline text for proration + tax clause.
- Tomorrow 10:00am PT: 30-min call to agree language and invoicing fields.
- After call: Redwood to deliver RW_OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx with agreed edits for Cloudly sign-off.

If that schedule works, Nina / Ari can send a Teams or Zoom invite for 10:00am PT tomorrow.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Order form — redlines and a few clarifying asks

Ari / Logan / team,

I reviewed Cloudly's redline and sketched proposed language below. This is intended to be inserted into the Order Form appendix and mirrored in the MSA where tax responsibility is described. Please consider this a starting point — happy to take edits on the call.

1) Minimum commit proration (proposed):
"If the Service Commencement Date falls on a date other than the first day of a calendar month, the Minimum Commitment for the first month will be prorated on a per-day basis using the calendar month in which services commence (number of active service days / number of days in month). Thereafter, full-month Minimum Commitments apply."

2) Invoicing cadence & net terms (commercial):
"Invoices will be issued monthly in arrears unless Customer requests quarterly invoicing in writing at least 30 days prior to the invoice period. Standard payment terms are Net 45 from date of invoice unless otherwise agreed in writing."

3) Taxes and withholding (key point):
"Unless otherwise required by applicable law, Customer is responsible for taxes, duties and governmental charges assessed on the Customer's purchase of services. In the event a taxing authority requires withholding of tax on payments to Redwood, Customer shall (a) provide evidence of withholding to Redwood within ten (10) business days of such requirement; (b) endeavor to obtain a tax treaty benefit or exemption where available; and (c) reimburse Redwood for any net amount withheld such that Redwood receives the full amount invoiced. Parties agree to cooperate in providing documentation (tax certificates, invoices with gross-up) necessary for refund or credit. Redwood will not accept liability for local withholding absent an explicit indemnity in the Order Form."

4) Invoice fields (for PO compatibility):
Required: Redwood legal entity name, Tax ID, Invoice number, Invoice date, PO number, Billing entity address, Remit-to bank wiring instructions (we'll share a sample).

Open item: Cloudly requested that Redwood accept withholding without gross-up in specific countries — that's a commercial exception; please confirm who on Cloudly's side owns that ask so Ben / Logan can confirm commercial trade-offs on margin.

I'll have a tracked-change document ready after the call; Logan will share.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
From: Ari Kaplan <ari@cloudly.com>

Date: 2028-05-18T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form — redlines and a few clarifying asks

Thanks Kimberly — the proposed language is clear and hits most of our needs. A couple of clarifications from Cloudly finance: 

- The pro-rata formula is acceptable. We will add a short sentence to the PO to indicate the desired start date to help avoid ambiguity.
- For withholding: we can accept a reimbursement / gross-up in principle but need a mechanism: either (a) Redwood provides a local invoice with gross-up and Cloudly remits the withheld amount to Redwood; or (b) Cloudly withholds and then issues evidence and pays an expedited gross-up within 30 days. Our FP&A team prefers (a) where feasible.
- PO fields: attached our PO_Instructions.pdf with required fields and mandatory billing address format.

We confirmed tomorrow's 10:00am PT call — invite sent. Looking forward to finalizing language and the sample invoice format.

Best,
Ari
